lifecycle.selection: Dedicated leavepilot-runtime-test compose fixture on loopback 13306/16379/16380 with the synthetic matrix inputs. Startup = spawn to first HTTP 200 on /login/ (listener cannot open before SQL and selected Store are ready). Shutdown = SIGTERM delivery to process exit. Outage detection/recovery are external polls at 50 ms granularity through a loopback RESP2 interrupting proxy; recovery keeps the same PID. Store initialize = createSessionMiddleware().sessionLifecycle.initialize() (RESP2 connect + public Store set/get/touch/destroy probe + cleanup). Worker replacement = SIGKILL of a serving worker to its replacement's first readiness report. No failed sample was discarded; every listed scenario exited as asserted.

scenarios.note: Real in-flight request with a trickled body; drain deadline at 8000 ms fired forced disposal and the stop completed at 8025 ms with the required nonzero incomplete exit.

policy.rationale: One absolute deadline covering SQL connect, schema check, selected Store initialize and listen, plus allowlisted transient retries. Observed cold/warm startup maximum is 472 ms across all twelve contours on the disposable fixture; the 20000 ms budget is deliberate headroom for container/CI hosts and in-window dependency retry, and it stays inside the existing 30000 ms bin/test.js readiness envelope with 10 s left for harness detection and cleanup. Reducing it would buy nothing and risk flapping slow hosts; the deadline-exceeded and never-settling startup paths exit nonzero without opening the listener (fault scenarios and t/unit/runtime_startup.js injected-clock cases).

Exponential floor for the four allowlisted transient connection codes, doubling to at most 1000 ms inside the single startup deadline. Healthy fixture boots never needed a retry (all cold startups succeeded first attempt), so 250 ms only paces retries against a just-restarting dependency; permanent auth/schema/config errors bypass retries entirely (fault-mysql-credentials-direct exited in 286 ms).

Preserves the pre-phase default envelope. Normal signal stops complete in at most 9 ms on every contour, so the 8000 ms drain window exists entirely for slow in-flight work; the real forced case hit the 8000 ms boundary, completed forced disposal in the reserved tail and exited 8025 ms later with code 1 (incomplete stop never reports success). Delayed close callbacks are checked against the absolute deadline in t/unit/runtime_shutdown.js with injected clocks and real subprocess watchdogs.

Bounded recovery window for the selected Redis-compatible store after a runtime loss, symmetric with the startup deadline per D-06. Real outages were detected within one 50 ms poll on Redis and Engram and recovered in 150-212 ms in the same PID after a successful public Store probe; the window is headroom for a realistic dependency restart, is never reset by reconnect attempts, and its expiry exits nonzero (t/runtime/redis_session_lifecycle.js deadline tracer).

Ceilings for one public Store callback and for a graceful client close. Healthy round-trips through the real middleware measured 8-10 ms including connect and the full probe; 1000 ms bounds blackholed in-flight commands and hung closes on degraded hosts while staying far below the recovery window (blackhole and close-fault cases covered by t/unit/middleware/session_lifecycle.js and the real lifecycle suite).

Three cumulative replacement attempts per worker slot with growing backoff. A real SIGKILLed worker was replaced and serving again in 544-600 ms (250 ms backoff plus boot); the sequence bounds crash-loop impact while tolerating three transient worker losses, and exhaustion stops peers with a nonzero cluster exit (t/unit/runtime_cluster.js supervisor cases).

The supervisor waits one full worker shutdown budget (10000 ms) plus 2000 ms of primary-side accounting before SIGKILL; observed supervisor stops completed in 8-11 ms after all workers drained, and the overdue-worker path escalates to SIGKILL with a 500 ms reserve and a nonzero exit (t/unit/runtime_cluster.js bounded-overdue case).
